summary: Gemini's Phase A design is compatible with CORE-001 requirements and the frontend-only architecture. It establishes a coherent design system, makes the Treatment Readiness Graph the signature experience, covers all required responsive surfaces and states, and preserves human clinical authority and caregiver data minimization.
review_scope: Compatibility only. Do not substitute Codex aesthetic preferences for Gemini design authority.
notes_for_gemini: Gemini retains full frontend visual and interaction authority within task scope: frontend/**, tests/frontend/**, docs/design/**, frontend-design-report.json, and frontend-report.json.

In production UI copy, represent the clinical branch as human clinical review/acknowledgment or disposition recorded; do not imply OncoReady medically cleared treatment, decided that treatment should proceed, or performed automated triage.

Keep the caregiver projection allowlisted to transportation status and assert that Maria's clinical concern and clinical-task details never enter Ana's rendered view or accessible name/description content.
Use aria-live for discrete workflow changes only; do not announce every countdown tick. Preserve stable semantic text for treatment proximity and status.

Treat stated WCAG conformance as an implementation target that must be verified, not a user-facing compliance claim. Preserve keyboard operation, visible focus, 44px touch targets, non-color state cues, and reduced-motion equivalence.
Any FHIR codes, staff identities, resource/driver details, delivery events, clinical protocols, or outcomes shown remain synthetic/simulated and must not be presented as live Ochsner integration.
The optional celebration dependency must remain lightweight, non-blocking, respectful of reduced motion, and removable if it adds bundle or reliability risk. It is not required for acceptance.
